# BiyaHey! — UX v2 design spec (Kalsada identity)

**Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Status:** approved direction (approach chosen in the mockup panel) · **Scope:** whole PWA
**Approved mockups:** `.superpowers/mockups/option-a-kalsada.html` (route options + trip detail states), generated by
`.superpowers/mockups/gen-ui-v2.mjs`.

## 1. Intent

The v1 PWA is functionally complete but visually crude: every route alternative is drawn in one
mode-ish colour so the map reads as a mush, the trip-detail screen has no map, cards have no leg
sequence, and copy/layout is inconsistent across screens. This pass makes BiyaHey! feel like a
production navigation app while keeping the civic-data honesty that differentiates it.

The human's brief:

- Take inspiration from **Moovit**: choosing a route must show **the different paths you will take**
  (each alternative as its own path, and the chosen itinerary drawn leg-by-leg).
- Do **as many passes as needed** until it reaches production standard for navigation apps.
- Apply a **full app + new visual identity** (approved: Option A "Kalsada", civic-modern).
- Turn the in-trip screen into a **leg-by-leg walkthrough** (no fake live data).
- **Playwright-test** the features.

Non-negotiable project constraints that survive this pass: no official PH GTFS/GTFS-RT exists, so
the app must never claim real-time data; every fare/attribution comes from the API (`R45`); the
first-screen JS payload stays ≤ 250 KB gzip; MapLibre stays lazy-loaded; the UI stays Taglish.

## 2. What changes, screen by screen

| Screen | Change |
|---|---|
| **Home** | Sheet redesign: wordmark + one-line promise, search pill first, **recent trips with leg strips** (from the existing 30-day recents store), saved + about-data doors. Honest empty state. |
| **Search / directions form** | Kalsada styling: From/To card with mode-neutral icons, swap, up to two via stops, device-location shortcut, one clear primary CTA; results grouped Stops/Landmarks/Routes with consistent rows; unchanged behaviour/URL contract (`tripParams.ts`). |
| **Route options** | Sheet header (eyebrow, `From → To`, departure line). New card anatomy: big ETA + arrival, badge, fare, **leg-strip ribbon**, transfers/walk meta, fare-provenance line. Selected card = brand ring + tinted surface; exactly one "Tingnan ang detalye" action under the selected card. **Map**: each alternative is its own path (own hue, thin, numbered marker 2..n); selected route is drawn leg-by-leg with mode colours, white casing, dashed walk legs, transfer dots, origin/destination pins. Selecting a card re-fits and re-emphasises the map; tapping an alternative path on the map selects its card. |
| **Trip detail** | Map header (collapsible via scroll) with the chosen itinerary drawn leg-by-leg; back/save/share controls floating. Summary: duration, arrival, fare/transfers/walk. Primary CTA "Simulan ang biyahe" + save. **Leg-strip ribbon as interactive progress rail**; step timeline restyled with mode-coloured icon rail, instruction, times/stops, "Hanapin" signage plate, expandable stop list, landmark line **only when the API sent one** (no more placeholder sentence). **Map ↔ timeline sync**: tapping a leg (row or strip segment) emphasises that leg on the map and zooms to it; tapping a leg line on the map highlights the row. Fare breakdown card restyled. Saved-snapshot warnings preserved. |
| **Live trip** (`/trip/:id/live`) | From static placeholder to **leg-by-leg walkthrough**: full route on the map with the current leg emphasised, "Hakbang N ng M", current-leg card (instruction, signage, next alight stop), prev/next controls, finished state. Explicit honest banner: walang live tracking; guided by the planned itinerary only. |
| **Saved** | Kalsada cards: real title from itinerary endpoints (`Cubao → Ayala`) instead of `START → END`, leg strip, ETA/fare/saved date, staleness banner, Buksan/Palitan/I-delete actions, empty/offline states. |
| **About data / licences** | Kalsada dataset cards, licence sheet, attribution chips; unchanged provenance content. |

## 3. Visual identity — "Kalsada" (civic-modern)

Brand seed teal, ink navy, warm fare amber, white cards on a pale sage canvas. One accent (teal) for
actions/brand; fare amber reserved for money; transit mode colours reserved for data.

### 3.1 Colour roles (light)

| Role | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `#F4F6F3` | page canvas |
| `surface-container-lowest` | `#FFFFFF` | cards, sheet, fields |
| `surface-container` | `#EAF0EB` | quiet chips, skeletons |
| `on-surface` | `#0B1D24` | primary text, active chip fill (`inverse` roles) |
| `on-surface-variant` | `#54656C` | secondary text |
| `outline-variant` | `#DAE2DF` | hairlines, dividers |
| `primary` | `#0E7C7B` | brand, CTA, selected ring |
| `primary-container` | `#D9EFEE` | selected tint, badge bg alternative |
| `inverse-surface` | `#0B1D24` | active filter chip / dark surfaces |
| `inverse-on-surface` | `#F4F6F3` | text on inverse |
| `fare-bg` | `#FFF1C9` | fare surfaces |
| `on-fare-bg` | `#4F3400` | fare text |
| `fare-border` | `#E7C265` | fare hairline |
| `error` | `#BA1A1A` | destructive |
| `focus-ring` | `#0E7C7B` | focus outline |

Dark scheme keeps the same role names with dark-tuned values (see `tokens.css`); the basemap stays
OpenFreeMap "Liberty" light in both schemes (documented performance/contrast trade-off).

### 3.2 Type, shape, elevation

- System sans only (Android-Go budget). Display numerals 800 weight, `tracking-tight`, tabular
  numerals; screen titles 700 20 px; card titles 700 15–16 px; body 14–16 px; eyebrow labels 10–11 px
  700 uppercase `tracking-[0.12em]`.
- Radius: cards/fields 20 px (`--shape-medium`), sheet 28 px (`--shape-large`), pills full. Option C's
  square look was rejected with the identity choice.
- Elevation: card `0 1px 2px rgba(9,29,36,.06), 0 8px 24px -12px rgba(9,29,36,.28)`; sheet
  `0 -10px 34px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.35)`; selected card adds a 2 px `primary-container` ring.

### 3.3 Mode palette (data, not theme)

| Mode | Colour | Map treatment |
|---|---|---|
| walk | `#4C5B62` | dashed 6 px / dash 2-2, grey |
| jeepney | `#0E7C7B` | solid 7 px |
| bus | `#B45309` | solid 7 px |
| mrt3 | `#1F5FBF` | solid 7 px |
| lrt1 | `#2E7D32` | solid 7 px |
| lrt2 | `#7B1FA2` | solid 7 px |
| ferry | `#1565C0` | solid 7 px |
| uv-express | `#C2410C` | solid 7 px |
| p2p | `#475569` | solid 7 px |

Selected itinerary always has a ~12–13 px white casing under the coloured line and transfer dots
(white 7 px ring, ink 4 px centre) where legs meet. Alternatives: 3.5 px line in the itinerary's
primary-mode hue at ~50 % opacity plus a numbered circular marker; the legend is the card strip, so
colour is never the only channel.

## 4. Interaction and state contract

### 4.1 Route options (`/plan`)
- Sheet detents stay `[96, half, expanded]`, initial `half`.
- `selectedId` = explicit selection or ranked lead (existing behaviour, kept).
- Card press selects (`aria-pressed`); the map re-emphasis and camera fit follow the same state.
- One detail action (48 dp) under the selected card navigates to `/trip/:id`.
- Filter chips re-rank locally (existing `rankItineraries` contract); the selected itinerary is kept
  by id when it is still present, otherwise falls back to the ranked lead.
- Map: initial camera fits all alternatives; on explicit selection, fit the selected itinerary
  (`duration: 450`, padding 48/96, respect `prefers-reduced-motion` → duration 0).

### 4.2 Trip detail (`/trip/:id`)
- State: `selectedLegIndex: number | null` (null = whole itinerary emphasis).
- Clicking a timeline row header or a strip segment sets/clears the leg; the map emphasises that leg
  (others at 30 % opacity, selected at full width + halo) and fits it; the row scrolls into view.
- Clicking a leg line on the map sets the same state (map remains pannable/zoomable).
- The summary, save CTA and saved-snapshot copy keep the current honesty rules (`R63`, mandated
  strings unchanged). `Start trip` → `/trip/:id/live`.
- Scrolling: map header is sticky/parallax under the content sheet; content is the scroll container;
  reduced motion respected.

### 4.3 Live walkthrough (`/trip/:id/live`)
- State machine: `stepIndex ∈ [0, legs.length-1]`, plus `finished`.
- Route drawn whole; current leg full emphasis, past legs dimmed brand-ink, future legs dimmed.
- Content: honest banner ("Walang live tracking…"), `Hakbang N ng M`, current leg instruction,
  signage plate, alight stop, time window; controls "Nakaraan" / "Susunod"; final step shows
  "Tapos ang biyahe" + exit.
- No geolocation permission is requested; no ETA is recalculated.

### 4.4 Home
- Recents come from `readRecentTrips()` (max 3 shown); row title = endpoints helper; tap opens
  `/trip/:id` (cache or saved); empty state invites a plan. No invented "nearby" data.

## 5. Component architecture

New/changed modules (all under `apps/web/src/`):

```
components/transit/
  modeMeta.tsx        MODE_COLORS, MODE_ICONS, KNOWN_MODES, isKnownMode, primaryMode (moved out of map)
  LegStrip.tsx        the leg ribbon (display + interactive progress rail); a11y list semantics
  LegStrip.test.tsx
components/map/
  RoutePathLayer.tsx  selected + alternative paths, casing, walk dashes, transfer dots, markers,
                      camera fit, selection + leg-focus interaction, DEV map hook
  RoutePathLayer.test.tsx
  RoutePolylines.tsx  (deleted; tests migrated)
  MapCanvas.tsx       + `__biyaheyMap` DEV handle, Marker-safe teardown
lib/
  format.ts           formatFare, transfersLabel, walkLabel, legDistanceLabel (shared)
  itinerary.ts        itineraryEndpoints(), leg helpers, leg mode sequence
features/…
  RouteCard v2, FilterChips v2, RouteOptionsScreen v2
  TripDetailScreen v2, LegTimeline v2, TripLiveScreen v2, FareBreakdown v2
  HomePage v2, SavedScreen v2, SearchScreen styling
i18n/strings.ts       new/changed keys (all screens; added up-front in foundation)
theme/tokens.css      Kalsada light + dark palettes, shape/elevation
tailwind.config.js    token mappings (inverse-surface/on-inverse already mapped; add radius/shadow updates)
```

Props of the map layer (frozen interface for parallel work):

```ts
interface RoutePathLayerProps {
  itineraries: readonly ItineraryDto[];
  /** shortlist: selected + numbered alternatives; detail/live: one itinerary only */
  variant?: 'shortlist' | 'detail';
  selectedId?: string | null;
  onSelect?: (id: string) => void;
  /** detail/live: emphasised leg; null = whole itinerary */
  activeLegIndex?: number | null;
  onSelectLeg?: (index: number) => void;
  /** camera fit target; default 'all' on first render, 'selected' after an explicit select */
  fit?: 'all' | 'selected' | 'active-leg' | 'none';
  /** reduced-motion aware animation */
  animated?: boolean;
}
```

Data flow stays: `usePlan` → `RouteOptionsScreen`/`plan.tsx` own filter + selection →
`RoutePathLayer` draws + reports map clicks. Trip detail reads `cachedTrip(id)` (or saved snapshot)
and owns `selectedLegIndex`.

## 6. Accessibility

- Every leg strip is an ordered list with a text equivalent (visually hidden): "4 min lakad, MRT-3, 5
  hintuan, 6 min lakad". Interactive strips expose each segment as a button with `aria-pressed` and
  `aria-label`.
- Card selection uses `aria-pressed`; leg focus uses `aria-current="step"`; the map is a labelled
  region and is never the only path to information.
- Contrast: body ≥ 4.5:1, large text ≥ 3:1, mode lines ≥ 3:1 against the basemap; badge text on mode
  colours ≥ 4.5:1 (verified in `theme/tokens.test.ts` for tokens and in the map palette test for
  mode colours).
- Targets ≥ 48 dp; focus rings always visible; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables camera animation and
  media transitions.
- Live-region announcements for: route selection ("Ruta 2 pinili"), leg focus ("Hakbang 2: …"),
  walkthrough step changes, save results.

## 7. Performance

- Keep the entry payload ≤ 250 KB gzip (`perf/bundle.test.ts`); no new runtime dependencies.
- MapLibre stays behind the existing lazy boundary; `RoutePathLayer` adds only GeoJSON sources/layers
  (few hundred vertices per plan).
- No web fonts; icons stay in `lucide-react`.
- Lighthouse remains PARTIAL (TBT) and is not made worse; re-run the recorded perf job and record the
  numbers in the acceptance runbook.

## 8. Testing and verification

- **Unit (Vitest/jsdom):** new components tested with the MapLibre double (extended with `Marker`);
  leg-strip semantics; RouteCard v2 content/selection; route-options re-rank + detail action; trip
  detail leg sync (row → map props and map → row); live walkthrough state machine; saved title;
  home recents; contrast/token tests.
- **Playwright (live stack):**
  - existing `plan-a-trip` flow updated for v2 selectors/behaviour;
  - `map-rendering.spec.ts` — asserts via a DEV `window.__biyaheyMap` handle that the selected path is
    drawn as leg-coloured features (walk dashed layer + ride layer), alternatives are drawn, card
    selection changes the rendered selection, and trip-detail leg focus changes the emphasised leg;
  - `ux-v2.spec.ts` — home recents, route-card selection ↔ map sync, detail leg sync, stops expander,
    live walkthrough advance/finish, saved trip title/actions, sources screen;
  - existing `service-worker.spec.ts` and `smoke.spec.ts` kept green.
- **Visual:** `docs/screenshots/*` regenerated from the built app with the existing screenshot script
  (updated to the new flow); every screen reviewed at 390×844 and desktop 1440×900.
- **Gates:** `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build --workspace @biyahey/web`,
  `npm run test:e2e`, and `npm run verify:phase2` (recorded PARTIAL wherever the pre-existing TBT
  ceiling fails).

## 9. Non-goals

- No new routing/API/data behaviour; no real-time claims; no geolocation-based trip following.
- No new routes/screens beyond those listed; no i18n locale picker.
- No redesign of `/sources` content, only styling.
- No change to the fare/fare-provenance contract.

## 10. Acceptance criteria

1. On `/plan`, every returned alternative is visible as its own path on the map; exactly one is the
   selected leg-coloured route; selecting a different card updates the map without a refetch.
2. Every route card and the trip-detail header shows a leg strip whose segments match the itinerary's
   legs (mode + relative duration) and whose colours match the map lines.
3. Trip detail shows a real map of the chosen itinerary; tapping any leg row or strip segment
   emphasises/zooms that leg, and tapping a map leg highlights its row.
4. The live screen walks through the legs with previous/next controls, an honest no-live-data banner,
   and a finished state.
5. Home shows up to three recent trips once they exist, with leg strips; saved trips are titled by
   their endpoints.
6. All gates in §8 pass (Lighthouse reported honestly, not green-washed); screenshots updated.
7. No regression to provenance, fare dates, saved-snapshot honesty, offline/SW behaviour, or the
   URL contract.
